# dsh-emotion-feedback

A DSH plugin that **judges the working model's *own* emotion
each turn and silently re-injects it be
fore the next turn starts.**
> Opposite direction from the usual "sense the user's mood, then adapt the reply" plugins: what is j

udged and
> fed back here is the *assistant's* own state — a loop of **self-observation → state carr
y-over → behavior shift**.

- Host plugin (`dsh.bundle`) + browser panel (`dsh.client`) in one package, no build step.
- Zero mo
del calls when the keyword layer hits; one lightweight call (temperature 0, single-line JSON) only o

therwise.
- Judging itself never reaches the transcript — the user sees the *next* turn's tone, not
dging itself never reaches the transcript — the user sees the *next* turn's tone, not the machinery.
## The loop
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Injection is idempotent per session per turn, and is skipped entirely below `minIntensity`.
## Emotion state
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- **Labels are never rewritten.** An older revision mapped unknown labels to `平静` ("calm"), which er

ased
every nuance the judge produced; now an out-of-vocabulary label is only flagged `outOfList: tru

e`.
The vocabulary is used for two things: the preferred options in the judge prompt and the legal l

abel set
of the keyword rules.
- **Negation guard.** A keyword hit is discarded when a negation word

(`不 / 没 / 无 / 非 / 避免 / 规避 / 降低 /
减少 / 最低 / 较低 / 可控`) appears near it — this blocks reverse hits suc

h as "不确定" or "风险可控".
Set `negations: []` to turn the guard off.
- **Blend, don't replace.** The old

intensity is first decayed by `turnDecay ^ turns-elapsed`, then:
same emotion → `max(old, new)`; em

otion switch → `max(old × takeoverRetain, new)`.
- **Idle decay is disabled.** Reading a snapshot us

ed to apply `0.5 ^ (idleMinutes / halfLifeMinutes)`; that
module is commented out (the original impl

ementation is kept in `rehydrate()` for reference and the
`halfLifeMinutes` field still exists but h
as no effect). Intensity now only moves through `blend()`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`dsh plugin add` runs `pnpm add`, verifies `dsh.bundle` in `package.json`, and merges `cordis.patch.

yml`
into the profile. The single `insert` row in `cordis.patch.yml` is the whole wiring:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> **DSH must be fully restarted.** Installation only merges the bundle patch layer into the config g

raph;
> plugin module loading and `apply()` happen while the host assembles the plugin generation. T

he browser half
> is a static bundle with no HMR, so a new browser tab is not enough.
>
> You can al

so install it from inside a DSH session by asking the agent to call the `plugin_manager` tool's
> `i
nstall_bundle` action with this directory.
`INSTALL.md` is a longer Chinese handoff guide (unpack → install → 5 self-checks → troubleshooting).
A Chinese version of this README lives in `README.zh.md`.
## Configuration
Give the plugin row a `config:` block in a profile patch; every field has a default.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Effect |

| `enabled` / `inject` | `true` | master switch / whether to inject (off = judge only) |
| `disabled

` | `false` | emergency switch, takes priority over `enabled`, no uninstall needed |
| `minIntensity

` | `0.2` | injection threshold |
| `judgeProvider` / `judgeModel` | `''` | judge target; falls back

to `agent.options` → session request header → session default model |
| `useLlm` | `true` | whether

the model judge layer is allowed |
| `timeoutMs` | `6000` | single judge timeout |
| `turnDecay` /

`takeoverRetain` | `0.9` / `0.35` | blend rules above |
| `halfLifeMinutes` | `10` | **inactive** (k

ept for reference only) |
| `injectPerStep` | `false` | also allow injection on later steps of the s

ame turn |
| `emotions` / `rules` / `prompt` / `template` | built-in | vocabulary (15 labels) / keyw

ord rules / judge prompt / injection text |
| `negations` | see above | negation word list; `[]` dis

ables the guard |
| `panelEvent` / `panelRoute` / `statusTool` | `true` | session event / read-only

HTTP route / `emotion_status` tool |
| `persistHistory` | `true` | write per-session history to disk

tion_status` tool |
| `persistHistory` | `true` | write per-session history to disk (kept 30 days) |
The full schema is `Config` in `lib/types/index.d.ts`.
## Surfaces
### Browser panel
Docked above the composer at the `conversation.composer.dock` slot, labelled "情绪" (emotion). Collaps

ed it is
a coloured dot + emotion + intensity; expanded it shows the intensity bar, the latest judge

(time, previous
emotion, reason, source `关键词`/`模型判定`, out-of-vocabulary flag, raw judge value and b

lend factor when the
host snapshot is reachable), a 40-point intensity curve, and the last 8 judgeme

factor when the
host snapshot is reachable), a 40-point intensity curve, and the last 8 judgements.

The panel needs **no extra endpoint**: every injection is written into the session log as
`user/mess

age` + `source.kind = 'emotion-feedback'` + `surfaceOp: 'append'`, and the browser half reads the
co
nversation nodes through the standard slot prop `useChat((s) => s.legacy.nodes)`. So the curve is li

terally
*what the model received*. The optional `GET /emotion-feedback/state?sessionId=…` route (Web

deployments)
only adds host-side detail; when it is unreachable the panel degrades silently.
### `emotion_status` tool (read-only)
Lets the *model* read its own current state: emotion, intensity, reason, source (`rule` / `llm`) and

the recent
trajectory. It reads the same in-process state as the panel. Registration is reactive
(`
ctx.inject(['tools'], …)`), and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is imported lazily, so a host without that

package
loses the tool and nothing else.
### History file

`<DSH_HOME>/emotion-feedback/history/<sessionId>.json` — per-turn judgement records, kept 30 days.
D
isable with `persistHistory: false`.
## Compatibility

- DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` (declared as an optional peer `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`).
- `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `

>=4.0.4 <5.0.0`; `@deepseek-ai/schemastery ~3.18.4` is the only runtime dependency.
- Node `^22.19.0
|| >=24.0.0`. No build step: `lib/index.js` (host) and `lib/client.js` (browser) ship as source.
